title: Intro to Design and Tech with AI
shortDescription: Foundations of design and technology, with AI as a creative partner.
longDescription: A comprehensive look at design and technology — color, typography, layout, user-centered research, prototyping, and the basics of HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Python. We'll bring AI in as a creative and analytical partner across the process so you leave with both fundamentals and a modern toolkit. Suits aspiring designers, engineers, entrepreneurs, or anyone curious about the field.
audience: Anyone curious about design and tech
location: The Loft 419, downtown Toledo (hybrid options available)

instructor.name: Michael Vanderpool
instructor.bio: Founder and instructor at AWID. Background in design, technology education, and applied innovation.

prerequisites: None — bring a laptop if you have one.
learningObjectives: Apply design fundamentals — color, typography, layout, composition
Conduct user research and design with personas and empathy
Use design thinking to frame and solve real problems
Prototype, test, and iterate based on user feedback
Build interactive designs with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
Use Python for data analysis, automation, and interactive elements
Make design decisions informed by real data
Use AI tools as a creative and analytical partner
Communicate design decisions clearly — verbally and visually

title: Introduction to a Career in Tech
shortDescription: Explore tech career paths, the skills they need, and how to break in.
longDescription: An overview course for anyone considering a career in technology — career changers, recent grads, or curious beginners. We'll cover the landscape of tech careers, the skills and certifications that matter, learning resources, and concrete steps to get started. You'll leave with a clear understanding of your potential path and a personal action plan.
location: The Loft 419, downtown Toledo (hybrid options available)

instructor.name: Michael Vanderpool
instructor.bio: Founder and instructor at AWID. Background in design, technology education, and applied innovation.

learningObjectives: Understand the tech industry landscape and demand
Identify the key skills and certifications for major roles
Compare paths across software, IT, cybersecurity, data, cloud, UX, and product
Choose between degrees, bootcamps, and self-taught routes
Build experience through projects, portfolios, and open source
Navigate the tech job search and interview process
Build a personalized action plan for entering the industry

title: AI Infused Game Design
shortDescription: Design and build a small game using AI-assisted tools.
longDescription: Students will work through the full arc of game design — concept, mechanics, art, and playtest — using AI tools as a creative partner. We finish with a playable mini-game.
location: The Loft 419, downtown Toledo (hybrid options available)

instructor.name: Michael Vanderpool
instructor.bio: Founder and instructor at AWID. Background in design, technology education, and applied innovation.

learningObjectives: Frame a game concept and define a core mechanic
Sketch level designs and iterate with AI assistance
Use AI tools to generate art, sound, and writing assets
Build a small playable game using a beginner-friendly engine
Run playtests and incorporate feedback into the next iteration
Reflect on AI as a creative partner versus a shortcut
Ship and demo a finished mini-game

title: Applied AI in Design Thinking
shortDescription: Learn the design thinking process — with AI as your creative and analytical partner from day one.
longDescription: A beginner-friendly introduction to design thinking — empathize, define, ideate, prototype, test — taught hands-on with AI tools woven into each phase of the process. No prior experience required. You'll learn the method and use it on a small real-world problem, leaving with a working prototype and a process you can apply to anything.
location: The Loft 419, downtown Toledo (hybrid options available)

instructor.name: Michael Vanderpool
instructor.bio: Founder and instructor at AWID. Background in design, technology education, and applied innovation.

learningObjectives: Understand each phase of design thinking — empathize, define, ideate, prototype, test
Conduct simple user research and synthesize what you find with AI assistance
Frame a clear, actionable problem statement from research insights
Run an ideation session that uses AI to expand the option space
Build a quick prototype using AI-assisted tools
Run a small test and incorporate feedback into the next iteration
Recognize where AI genuinely helps the process — and where it can mislead
Take a small problem from empathy through prototype within the workshop
